name: Meat Offerings
overview: The meat offering, as described in Scripture, is a finely prepared gift of fine flour mixed with oil and frankincense, set apart as a sweet savor to the LORD and offered by fire on the altar of burnt offering (Leviticus 2:1; Exodus 40:29). These offerings were part of a continual burnt offering ritual, including morning and evening presentations, symbolizing ongoing dedication and communion with God (Exodus 29:40-42). Importantly, meat offerings were distinct from incense and were not to be presented on the altar of incense, underscoring their unique role in worship (Exodus 30:9).
